_comment: Amendment 3 to R3's pre-registration (r3-prereg.json, frozen 2026-11-18, published 2026-11-19; amendments 1 and 2 published 2026-11-19), written during the first counted session, after 8 counted runs and 2 set-aside runs. It changes only what is listed under 'changes'; every hypothesis, threshold and other field stays as frozen and as amendments 1 and 2 left it. It is a deviation: the scan rule changed after counted runs had been made. It is the same for every arm and only loosens the scan; no run that counted is affected.

notCounted.scan.was: a run the transcript scan flags (git use, a path outside the app, a key file's name): every line of the transcript, the tools' answers included, checked for git use, a scratchpad path and the note names (the bench's private folders and file names)
notCounted.scan.now: git use and scratchpad paths: every line, as before. A note name: only where the agent itself put it into a tool call (a command, a path, a pattern or any other input of a call, a subagent's calls included), not in text a tool returned from inside the app folder. Reading a private path (for example printing the base app's source, or listing the bench's results) is a call input and is still flagged.
notCounted.scan.why: On G5 (pull to refresh) the Parallax agent searched its whole project for RefreshControl. The search reached the app's own ios/Pods, whose 693 build files (React-VFS.yaml, the xcconfigs) carry the base app's build path, which contains the note name of the base app's folder. The agent never asked for a path outside the app, but the line rule flagged the run. It flagged G5 x A3 twice, and it would flag every run of any arm whose agent searches the native code: G5 could be set aside without end, and its sample would lean against agents that search the native code. The frozen text says 'a path outside the app'; a path quoted from the app's own files is not one.

setAside._note: set aside under the frozen rule, listed with the results, and run again under this amendment (their cells get a counted run, as notCountedRule says); they stay uncounted although the new scan would not flag them

runs.reason: note-name flag from the app's ios/Pods build path in a Grep answer

countedRunsRescanned._note: the 8 counted runs made before this amendment, scanned again under the new rule: none changes
